slides.title: Walking Down the Mountain 🏔️
slides.content:
# Gradient Descent Intuition

Imagine being blindfolded on a foggy mountain and wanting to reach the lowest valley. At every step, you feel the slope with your feet and step in the direction of steepest descent.

### The Parameter Update Rule:
$$
w := w - \alpha \frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial w}
$$

* **$\alpha$ (Learning Rate):** The size of the step taken downhill.
* **$\frac{\partial \mathcal{L}}{\partial w}$ (Gradient):** The direction and magnitude of steepest ascent.

```
Too Small alpha:                Optimal alpha:                 Too Large alpha:
Very slow convergence;         Smooth, steady descent         Overshoots and diverges
gets stuck in local minima.    to the global minimum.         wildly into infinity!
```

quizData.question: What commonly happens if your optimizer's learning rate is configured several orders of magnitude too high?

options.text: The model trains instantly in 1 step
The weights explode or diverge, and loss becomes NaN/infinite
The network automatically prunes all dead neurons
The training set size is doubled automatically

quizData.explanation: An excessively high learning rate overshoots the minimum of the loss valley, stepping uphill and causing explosive instability (gradient explosion / NaN loss).
